summary.text: A 28-year-old woman at 35 weeks of gestation from Loreto, Peru had four months of progressive dysphonia, 5 kg weight loss, dry cough and dysphagia, then odynophagia, fever, night sweats and productive cough one month before admission. She was admitted to the emergency room with respiratory distress and hemoptysis, bringing a laryngoscopy report that concluded laryngeal cancer, although no biopsy had been performed.

Examination showed bad general condition, tachypnea, dysphonia, decreased subcutaneous tissue, temperature 39 °C and increased heart and respiratory rates. Laryngeal cancer and laryngeal tuberculosis were proposed as differential diagnoses. A new laryngoscopy showed a mamelonated laryngeal tumoration with irregular vocal cords of limited mobility. Sputum bacilloscopy was positive and chest radiography showed bibasal nodular lesions and left apical opacities, raising high suspicion of laryngeal tuberculosis secondary to lung infection. Laryngeal biopsy was not possible.

Empirical isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide and ethambutol were started. After a week she improved, with resolution of fever, dyspnea, cough and dysphonia, which the authors say confirmed the presumptive diagnosis of laryngeal tuberculosis, and she was discharged with advice to continue treatment with ambulatory control. Later smears were negative from the second month, she was considered healed, and no adverse reactions or serious sequelae were reported.
